title: Negative: seasonal fuel regrowth does not make the layered CIPS condensates die selectively; mild famines change nothing and short total famines shrink every body to a core that regrows in place
summary: Aim: continued births need deaths, and the fed layered CIPS world has none (division stops when the box fills). world.py = c40's layered world plus a square-wave fuel regrowth (kF for 2000-f*2000 t, kF*lo for f*2000 t, from t=6000), 128x128, seed 0, T=20000. lo=0.25 and 0.5 (f=0.5): 7 bodies throughout, 0 deaths, 2 splits (ts_lo25.png, ts_lo50.png). lo=0 for 30 t or 50 t per 2000 t: every body shrinks together (occupancy 0.088 -> 0.006-0.01 in a 50 t famine) and all regrow from their cores at the same sites within ~200 t of the fuel's return; no body is lost for good, so there is no selective death (ts_pulse0.025.png, ts_pulse0.015.png).

finding.control: same world without seasons (7 bodies, 128x128, seed 0)
finding.result: lo 0.25/0.5: no deaths; total famine 30-50 t: all bodies shrink to cores and regrow in place, no permanent deaths

limits: One seed, a 128x128 box (7 bodies), one period (2000 t). Famines between 50 and 100 t (where some bodies might die and others recover) were not scanned; a 100 t total fork kills all bodies (c40).
